  "reasoning": "Every question has its own captured worked solution stating the mathematically correct answer, and every stated answer matches a current choice. q-210742: substituting u=ln(x³), with du=3 dx/x, gives u²+C on x>0. q-31329: substituting u=log₂x gives (ln 2)u²/2+C on x>0. q-31401: substituting u=log₃(x²), with du=2 dx/(x ln 3), gives (ln 3)u²/4+C on either interval excluding zero. q-13845: substituting u=ln(4x) gives one quarter of the integral of 1/u from ln 4 to 1, yielding −ln(ln 4)/4; the reversed bounds explain its negative sign. q-73664: the exponent has derivative −6x², so the antiderivative is −e^(5−2x³)+C. q-113847: the exponent has derivative −4x³, so the antiderivative is −2e^(4−x⁴)+C. q-73801: substituting u=x²+1 gives 6^u/ln 6+C. q-31420: substituting u=3x² gives 8^u/(6 ln 8)+C. q-31478 and q-31480: substituting the denominator gives its natural logarithm divided by the logarithm of the exponential base; both denominators are positive. q-114288: integration by parts with u=4x and v=e^(8x)/8 gives xe^(8x)/2−e^(8x)/16+C. q-12560: integration by parts with u=x+7 and v=e^(2x+5)/2 gives (x+7)e^(2x+5)/2−e^(2x+5)/4+C. q-74090: integration by parts gives 10x sin(x)+10 cos(x)+C. q-114314: integration by parts with v=−cot(x) gives −x cot(x)+ln|sin(x)|+C on intervals where sin(x) is nonzero. q-49674: x cos(2x) is odd, so its integral over symmetric bounds is zero. q-49660: evaluating −(x+1)e^(−x) at zero and −2 gives −1−e².
